title: The world continues past the nearest objects
note: Past the nearest objects the world must visibly continue: a path leaving, fields, roofs, hills — not an empty horizon.
intent: A place that stops at the last building tells the player they are on a set. Give the middle and far distance something: a lane or track leaving the frame, low-detail roofs or trees beyond the near cluster, a hill line or treeline silhouette against the sky, fields or water. It can be almost free — billboards, instanced low-poly masses, a painted ridge on the sky dome — because nobody walks there; what matters is that every eye-height camera has something beyond the near objects. Do not fake it with fog alone: fog hides an empty horizon, it does not make one continue.

check.ask: Beyond the nearest buildings or objects, does the world visibly continue (a path leaving, fields, trees, hills, more buildings) rather than ending in bare ground or an empty horizon?
check.note: Extent, from the player's eye at spawn: the place must read as part of a larger world.

port: The world facet builds a far ring after the near cluster and checks it from eye:spawn, the camera the critic uses.
